To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the covariance matching and AR methods are shown to be effective for DOA estimation in the presence of multiple scattering.

(1) the DOA estimation problem of multiple scattered sources in wireless communications can be formulated as a problem of estimating a covariance matrix from a reduced-size statistic; and (2) the covariance matching method and AR modelling of the reduced-size statistic are computationally efficient and nearly as good as the optimal maximum likelihood method.
(i) The AR-based estimator has performance close to that of the covariance-based estimator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of DOA estimation algorithms that are based on covariance matching of the reduced-size statistics obtained by averaging the sample covariance matrix over redundant samples.
the development of computationally efficient algorithms for DOA estimation in the presence of multipath.
the development of computationally efficient and robust methods for DOA estimation of multiple sources in scattering environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
covariance matching applied to the coherence loss function provides the best performance in terms of the mean square error (MSE) of the DOA estimate, followed by the AR-based estimator, and the CRB.

the AR-based method is a very good choice for DOA estimation when the number of snapshots is small, and the covariance matching approach is a very good alternative when the number of available snapshots is large.
the covariance matching approach is superior to AR-based methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a computationally efficient DOA estimation technique that is capable of providing high resolution and high accuracy estimates of DOA in the presence of multiple scattered sources.
we have proposed and developed computationally efficient algorithms for estimating the DOA of multiple scattered sources based on the sample covariance matrix.

the proposed AR-based estimator has the following advantages over the covariance matching method: (1) It is computationally efficient; (2) The AR-based estimator is a closed-form expression and does not require the iterative solution of a non-linear optimization problem; (3) It is applicable to any array geometry; and (4) The CRB of the AR-based estimator can be derived in a straightforward manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the presence of scatter, the DOA estimation performance can be significantly enhanced by using a reduced-size statistic that is derived after averaging over the redundant degrees of freedom of the sample covariance matrix.
the CRB can provide a useful tool for assessing the performance of DOA estimators in the presence of scattering.
, by using a reduced-size statistic, the problem of estimating DOA in the presence of scattering is reduced to a problem similar to that in the case of line-of-sight propagation.
